Population pyramid typical of a developing country like Nigeria. The vertical y-axis in the middle shows age groups (0-4, 5-9, up to 80+). The horizontal x-axis shows population size for Males on the left (blue bars) and Females on the right (pink bars). The overall shape is a broad-based triangle, very wide at the bottom representing young dependents, and narrowing sharply to a point at the top representing the elderly. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Demographic Transition Model graph. The x-axis represents time divided into four vertical sections labeled Stage 1 to Stage 4. The y-axis represents rate per 1,000 people. A red line for Death Rate starts high and fluctuating in Stage 1, plunges downward in Stage 2, and flattens out low in Stages 3 and 4. A blue line for Birth Rate starts high in Stage 1, stays high through Stage 2, falls steadily in Stage 3, and flattens out low in Stage 4. A green line for Total Population starts low, curves up steeply through Stages 2 and 3, and levels off very high in Stage 4. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
